help.appearance.assign: Gives the selected bodies, faces or components a color or a material look, without changing their weight. Use it to tell parts apart or to preview a finish.
help.assembly.bom: Lists the parts of the design or a component with their counts, by part number, and can save the list as CSV or JSON. Use it as the parts list for ordering and assembly.
help.canvas.decal: Places an image on a planar face of the model, like a sticker. Use it to show a label, logo or printed pattern on a part.
help.canvas.edit: Changes a canvas: its position, size, angle, opacity, mirroring, visibility or name. Use it to line up a reference image with the sketch you trace over it.
help.canvas.insert: Places a PNG or JPEG image on a plane or face as a see-through reference. Use it to trace a photo or drawing in a sketch, with the image scaled to a known size.
help.component.break_link: Cuts a linked component loose from its design file, keeping its bodies as they are. Use it when the part should no longer follow changes to the original file.
help.component.capture_position: Keeps the positions of parts you moved by hand, so they become where those parts are. Use it after dragging parts into place that no joint holds.
help.component.create: Adds a new, empty component to the design, inside the active component unless you choose another parent. Use it to give a new part of an assembly its own place for bodies and sketches.
help.component.finish_edit: Saves the part you are editing in place, returns to its assembly and updates the assembly from it. Use it when your changes to the linked part are done.
help.component.from_bodies: Turns each selected body into a component of its own, named after the body. Use it when a design built as loose bodies should become an assembly whose parts can be joined and moved.
help.component.insert_design: Inserts another saved design as a component linked to its file, with its solid bodies placed as they are there. Use it to reuse a part in an assembly and pick up later changes with Update Links.
help.component.properties: Shows the volume, mass, centre of mass and moments of inertia of a component, using its bodies' materials. Use it to check weight and balance of an assembly.
help.component.revert_position: Puts parts you moved by hand back where they were, dropping moves that were not captured. Use it to undo trial moves in an assembly.
help.component.update_links: Reads the linked design files again and replaces bodies where they changed. Use it after editing a part that this assembly uses.
help.config.configure: Adds parameters, features, materials or appearances as columns of the configuration table. Use it to build variants of one design, such as sizes of a part.
help.config.preview: Checks that a row of the configuration table rebuilds, without changing the design or its history. Use it before switching to a variant you are not sure of.
help.config.rules: Shows the rules of the configuration table, its rows and which row is active. Use it to see how the variants of a design are set up.
help.config.table: Shows the configuration table: one row per variant, one column per parameter or feature, and whether the design still matches the active row. Use it to review the variants of a design.
help.connect_note: Restart each assistant to load the SolidCraft server. Each file was backed up as .bak before it changed.
help.construct.axis.edge: Creates a construction axis along a straight edge or sketch line. Use it as the axis for a revolve, a circular pattern or a joint.
help.construct.axis.normal_to_face: Creates a construction axis through a point, square to a face. Use it as an axis that stands straight out of a surface.
help.construct.axis.through_cylinder: Creates a construction axis through the centre of a cylinder, cone or torus face, or a circular edge. Use it to turn or pattern features around a round part.
help.construct.axis.two_planes: Creates a construction axis where two planes or flat faces meet. Use it when the axis you need is the line between two faces.
help.construct.axis.two_points: Creates a construction axis through two points, vertices or sketch points. Use it for an axis that runs between two known positions.
help.construct.plane.along_path: Creates a construction plane square to an edge or curve, at a position along it. Use it to sketch a profile for a sweep or a section of a path.
help.construct.plane.at_angle: Creates a construction plane turned by an angle from a plane or face, about an axis or edge. Use it for sloped sketches, such as an angled bracket.
help.construct.plane.axis_point: Creates a construction plane containing an axis and a point off that axis. Pick an origin or construction axis, a straight edge or sketch line, then a vertex, sketch point or construction point. A point on the axis cannot define a unique plane.
help.construct.plane.midplane: Creates a construction plane halfway between two planes or flat faces, or bisecting them where they meet at an angle. Use it as a symmetry plane for mirroring.
help.construct.plane.offset: Creates a construction plane parallel to a plane or flat face, at a distance or through a point. Use it to sketch at a set height above a face.
help.construct.plane.perpendicular: Creates a construction plane that holds a line or edge and stands square to a plane or face. Use it to sketch upright on a model along an edge.
help.construct.plane.tangent: Creates a construction plane that touches a cylinder, cone, sphere or torus at a point. Use it to sketch on the side of a round part.
help.construct.plane.three_points: Creates a construction plane through three points. Use it for a plane set by positions on the model, such as three corners.
help.construct.plane.two_edges: Creates a construction plane through two straight edges or lines that lie in one plane. Use it for a plane across a part, such as through two opposite edges.
help.construct.point.along_path: Creates a construction point at a position along an edge or curve. Use it as a reference partway along a path.
help.construct.point.center: Creates a construction point at the centre of a circular edge, sketch circle or arc, sphere or torus. Use it as a reference for holes, axes and joints.
help.construct.point.edge_plane: Creates a construction point where an edge or line passes through a plane or flat face. Use it to mark where a path crosses a plane.
help.construct.point.three_planes: Creates a construction point where three planes or flat faces meet. Use it as a corner reference, even where the model has no vertex.
help.construct.point.two_edges: Creates a construction point where two edges or lines meet, or come closest. Use it as a reference at a virtual corner.
help.construct.point.vertex: Creates a construction point on a vertex or sketch point. Use it as a reference that stays when the sketch or body around it is hidden.
help.contact.check: Lists the pairs of parts in contact sets that pass through each other in their current position. Use it to find collisions before you drive joints or run a motion study.
help.contact.create: Groups two or more parts into a contact set, whose bodies are kept from passing through each other while joints move. Use it for parts that should stop when they touch, such as a lever against its stop.
help.contact.disable_all: Turns contact off, so driven joints and motion studies no longer stop where parts touch. Use it to move parts freely again, or to keep a large assembly responsive.
help.contact.edit: Changes a contact set: the parts it holds, its name, or whether it is suppressed; it can also delete the set. Use it to adjust which parts are kept from passing through each other.
help.contact.enable_all: Puts every part of the assembly into one contact set, so no two parts can pass through each other while joints move. Use it for a quick check of a whole mechanism.
help.contact.enable_sets: Turns contact on for the contact sets you defined, so driven joints and motion studies stop where their parts would pass through each other. Use it to bring your sets back after turning contact off.
help.contact.list: Lists the contact sets of the design, the parts in each one and whether contact is on. Use it to check how contact is set up before you drive the assembly.
help.document.inspect: Shows an overview of the design: its components, bodies, sketches, features and parameters. Use it to get your bearings in a design you did not build yourself.
help.document.units: Changes the units the design shows lengths in, such as mm or inches. The geometry keeps its size; only the display and plain numbers follow.
help.edit.checkpoint: Remembers the design, the active sketch and the undo history as they are now. Use it before trying something risky that you may want to go back from.
help.edit.restore_checkpoint: Goes back to a checkpoint, undo history included. Use it to drop everything done since the checkpoint in one step.
help.explode.create: Creates an exploded view that pushes the parts away from the assembly's centre, or by the moves you set. Use it to show how an assembly goes together, for instructions or presentations.
help.face.delete: Removes the selected faces and lets the neighboring faces close the gap, or leaves the gap open as a surface. Use it to take off a rounded edge, a hole or a boss that is in the way.
help.file.insert_mesh: Adds a 3MF, STL, OBJ, PLY or glTF file to the design as mesh bodies in a new component. Use it to place a downloaded or scanned model beside your design as a reference.
help.file.insert_step: Adds a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD or Rhino file to the design as solid bodies in a new component; an assembly's parts become nested components. Use it to bring in models from suppliers or other CAD programs.
help.file.save_mesh: Saves bodies as an STL, 3MF or OBJ mesh, with the smoothness of curved faces you choose. Use it to prepare parts for 3D printing or for programs that read meshes.
help.file.send_to_slicer: Saves the selected bodies as a 3MF file and opens it in the slicer you choose. Use it to go from the model to printing in one step.
help.font_details: The interface uses egui's built-in fonts (Ubuntu Light and Hack, under the Ubuntu Font Licence and the MIT/Bitstream Vera license; Noto Emoji and the emoji icon font, under the OFL and MIT). Sketch text uses Liberation Sans (SIL OFL 1.1). The Crafting Apps' optional font pack, craft-fonts (BIZ UDPGothic, Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC, Noto Sans Arabic; SIL OFL 1.1), is not bundled in SolidCraft builds.
help.frame.member: Places a profile, such as a tube or an aluminium extrusion, along the lines of a frame sketch, one member per line. Use it to build frames, racks and welded structures.
help.inspect.accessibility: Colours the faces a tool can reach from one direction, and those it cannot. Use it to check a part for machining or moulding from that side.
help.inspect.center_of_mass: Shows the centre of mass of bodies, each on its own and all together, at uniform density. Use it to check balance and where a part will tip.
help.inspect.colored_components: Gives each component its own temporary colour, without changing appearances. Use it to tell the parts of an assembly apart at a glance.
help.inspect.compare: Compares two bodies and shows where one has material the other does not, with volume and deviation. Use it to check a changed or imported part against the original.
help.inspect.continuity: Checks how smoothly faces meet along their edges: gaps, kinks or curvature jumps, and shades the seams. Use it to find where surfaces do not join cleanly.
help.inspect.curvature_comb: Draws combs along curves, edges or faces whose teeth show how strongly they bend. Use it to spot flat spots, kinks and uneven curvature.
help.inspect.curvature_map: Colours faces by how strongly they curve, red where the radius is small. Use it to find tight spots and to judge how smooth a surface is.
help.inspect.draft: Colours faces by their draft angle to a pull direction, marking those with too little. Use it to check a part before moulding or casting.
help.inspect.environment_map: Shows the model with a reflective, mirror-like finish. Use it to judge the flow of surfaces by the way reflections run across them.
help.inspect.interference: Finds bodies that overlap and shows each overlap with its volume. Use it to check an assembly for parts that collide.
help.inspect.isocurve: Draws the isoparametric curves of faces, the grid the surface is built on. Use it to see how a surface flows and where it bunches up.
help.inspect.measure: Measures lengths, distances, angles, areas and radii between what you pick, or the volume and mass of bodies. Use it to check sizes and clearances.
help.inspect.minimum_radius: Finds the smallest radius of curvature of curves, edges or faces, and where it is. Use it to check that a tool or nozzle can follow the shape.
help.inspect.section: Cuts the view open along a plane and hatches the cut faces, without changing the model. Use it to look inside parts and assemblies.
help.inspect.zebra: Shows black and white stripes reflected on the model's faces. Use it to judge smoothness: stripes that break or kink at an edge show a poor transition.
help.joint.as_built: Joins two parts where they already are, without moving either one, and sets how they may still move. Use it for parts you have already placed in their final position.
help.joint.cam: Links a turning cam to a follower, so the follower slides or swings as the cam's outline passes under it. Use it for cams, eccentrics and valve drives.
help.joint.create: Joins two parts at the joint origins you pick and moves the second part into place; the joint type sets how they may still move. Use it to build an assembly whose parts move like the real mechanism.
help.joint.drive: Sets a joint's angle or distance and moves the parts with it, within its limits; linked joints and closed loops follow. Use it to check that a mechanism moves as intended.
help.joint.gear: Links two turning joints with a gear ratio, so driving one turns the other. Use it for spur and ring gears, with the ratio from pitch radii or tooth counts.
help.joint.limits: Sets how far a joint may turn or slide, as a minimum and a maximum, or clears those limits. Use it to keep a hinge, slider or lever within its real range of travel.
help.joint.motion_link: Couples two joints with a ratio and an offset, so driving one moves the other. Use it for a fixed relation between joints that Gear, Rack and Pinion or Screw do not cover.
help.joint.origin: Places a named joint origin on a part: at the centre of a face or round end, the middle of an edge, a corner or a point. Use it to prepare where joints attach; one picked on a face follows it when the part changes size.
help.joint.rack_pinion: Links a turning pinion to a sliding rack, so the rack moves by the length of pitch circle the pinion rolls through. Use it for rack drives, steering and linear stages.
help.joint.reach: Moves a point on a part toward a target by changing the joints on its chain, within their limits. Use it to pose a mechanism by where its end should be, such as the tip of a robot arm.
help.joint.rigid_group: Locks the selected parts together as they are, so they move as one. Use it for parts that belong together and have no motion between them.
help.joint.screw: Links turning and sliding by a pitch, so each turn advances by that distance. Use it for lead screws, bolts and threaded spindles.
help.library.apply: Applies a material or appearance from a local library file to bodies, faces or components. Use it to reuse materials you saved from another design.
help.library.export: Saves the design's materials and appearances to a library file. Use it to share them or reuse them in other designs.
help.library.inspect: Checks a library file and lists its materials and appearances, without changing the design. Use it to see what a library holds before applying it.
help.material.assign: Sets what the selected bodies are made of, such as steel, aluminum or ABS. Use it so that the mass and weight match the real part.
help.material.properties.validate: Checks a material data card for consistent numbers and missing values. Use it before relying on the data for mass or stiffness.
help.mesh.convert: Rebuilds a mesh body, such as an STL, as an editable solid with flat and cylindrical faces. Use it to modify imported mechanical parts like a modelled body.
help.motion.study: Sets joint values at steps along a timeline and plays them back as an animation. Use it to watch a mechanism move through a sequence and check clearances along the way.
help.motion.trace: Traces the path a point on a part follows while a motion study plays or a joint is driven, and keeps it as a 3D sketch curve when you confirm. Use it to see where a mechanism reaches, or to build on its path.
help.occurrence.ground: Fixes a part in place, or frees it again, so that joints move the other parts around it. Use it for the frame or base that the rest of the assembly is built on.
help.occurrence.move: Moves an assembly part only along freedoms allowed by its joints. Select a part face, then drag an available arrow or arc.
help.parameters.change: Opens the table of named values and expressions that drive the dimensions of the design. Use it to change a size in one place and let every feature that uses it follow.
help.parameters.export: Saves the design's parameters as CSV or JSON. Use it to edit them in a spreadsheet or move them to another design.
help.parameters.graph: Shows which parameters and features use which others, and any loops or errors among them. Use it to see what a change to a parameter will affect.
help.parameters.import: Reads parameters from CSV or JSON into the design, all or none of them. Use it to bring in values from a spreadsheet or another design.
help.parameters.move: Moves a user parameter before or after another in the list. Use it to keep related parameters together.
help.parts.fastener: Adds a standard screw, bolt, nut, washer, pin or bearing in the size you pick. Placed on a hole, it seats in the hole with a joint, so you need not model fasteners yourself.
help.parts.insert: Inserts a standard part in the family, size and length you pick. Placed on the rim or wall of a hole, it seats on the hole with a rigid joint.
help.parts.library: Opens the standard parts: screws, bolts, nuts, washers, set screws, dowel pins and bearings in standard sizes. Use it to add a standard part instead of modelling it yourself.
help.parts.resize: Changes the size or length of an inserted standard part and rebuilds it; its joints keep it seated. Use it when a screw turns out too long or a hole needs another size.
help.plastic.assign_rule: Assigns a plastic rule to bodies, so their plastic features take its draft and clearance as defaults. Use it to set up a moulded part once for all its features.
help.plastic.boss: Adds a screw boss on a face: a post with an optional hole, draft, root fillet and supporting ribs. Use it for screw points in moulded or printed housings.
help.plastic.lip: Adds a lip or a matching groove along the rim of a shelled body. Use it so that two housing halves locate on each other and close tightly.
help.plastic.manage_rules: Creates and edits plastic rules: material, wall thickness, radii, clearance and draft. Use them to keep the features of a moulded part consistent.
help.plastic.rest: Adds a rest on a face: a round or rectangular pad, solid or hollow, with draft. Use it as a support or standoff in a moulded housing.
help.plastic.snap_fit: Adds a snap-fit hook on a face, with its length, thickness and catch. Use it to clip parts together without screws.
help.pointcloud.insert: Insert a PLY, XYZ or PTS scan as a point cloud alongside the model. Use it as a reference when building a model from measured data.
help.sheet.convert: Turns a plate or shelled body of even thickness into a sheet metal body, with bends at the edges you pick. Use it to make an existing part unfoldable.
help.sheet.export_bend_table: Saves the bend table of a sheet metal body as CSV or JSON: angles, radii and bend positions in the flat. Use it for the press brake or the workshop.
help.sheet.export_dxf: Saves the flat pattern as a DXF, with outlines, bend lines and optional bend notes. Use it for laser, plasma or waterjet cutting.
help.sheet.flange: Adds a flange: a base plate from a sketch, a wall along an open sketch contour, or a bent wall on sheet edges. Use it to build up sheet metal parts.
help.sheet.flat_pattern: Creates the flat pattern of a sheet metal body, with its size, cut-outs and bend lines. Use it to check the blank before you cut it.
help.sheet.fold: Bends a sheet along a sketch line by an angle and radius. Use it to fold a flat sheet after cutting features into it.
help.sheet.hem: Folds a sheet edge back on itself. Use it for safe, stiff edges without sharp burrs.
help.sheet.manage_rules: Creates and edits sheet metal rules: thickness, bend radius, K-factor, reliefs and gaps. Use them to match the material and tools of your workshop.
help.sheet.path_flange: Adds a chain of flanges along a sheet edge, following an open chain of sketch lines. Use it for profiles such as a U or Z shape in one step.
help.sheet.perforate: Adds a field of holes over the whole flat sheet, in a staggered or square pattern. Use it for vents, grilles and lighter panels.
help.sheet.refold: Folds an unfolded sheet metal body back up. Use it after adding features to the flat sheet.
help.sheet.unfold: Unfolds all bends of a sheet metal body. Use it to add holes or cuts that have to cross a bend, then refold.
help.sketch.arc.center_point: Draws a circular arc around a centre point, from a start point to an end point. Use it when the arc's centre is known, such as a radius around a hole or a pivot.
help.sketch.arc.tangent: Draws an arc that starts at the end of a line or arc and continues tangent to it. Use it to carry on a chain with a smooth bend instead of a corner.
help.sketch.arc.three_point: Draws an arc from a start point to an end point through a third point. Use it when the arc has to pass through given points rather than around a known centre.
help.sketch.arc3d: Draws an exact circular arc in space through three points, with 3D Sketch on. Use it for bends in paths and guide rails that leave the sketch plane.
help.sketch.auto_constrain: Adds the constraints the sketch nearly has already, such as horizontal, parallel or coincident, then dimensions it until it is fully defined. Use it to lock a roughly drawn sketch in one step.
help.sketch.auto_constrain_from_datum: Works like AutoConstrain, but measures the positions from a datum point you pick instead of the origin. Use it when the part is laid out from one reference point, such as a corner or a hole.
help.sketch.blend_curve: Joins the ends of two curves with a smooth spline that is tangent to both, or also curvature continuous if you choose. Use it to bridge a gap between curves without a kink.
help.sketch.break: Splits a curve into pieces where other curves cross it, or at points you place on it. Use it when part of a curve needs its own constraint or should be deleted on its own.
help.sketch.cancel: Leaves the sketch and discards everything changed since it was created or opened for editing. Undo brings the changes back.
help.sketch.centerline: Switches lines between normal lines and centerlines, axes that profiles leave out. Use a centerline as the axis for a revolve, a mirror or a symmetry constraint.
help.sketch.chamfer.distance_angle: Bevels the corner between two lines, set by a distance along the first line and an angle. Use it when a drawing gives the chamfer as a length and an angle, such as 2 mm × 30°.
help.sketch.chamfer.equal_distance: Bevels the corner between two lines the same distance back along both. Use it for the usual 45° chamfer on an outline.
help.sketch.chamfer.two_distance: Bevels the corner between two lines, set by a separate distance along each line. Use it for chamfers that are not 45°, given as two lengths.
help.sketch.circle.center: Draws a circle from its centre and its diameter. Use it for holes, bosses and other round features whose centre is known.
help.sketch.circle.three_point: Draws a circle through three points. Use it when the circle has to pass through given points, for example of existing geometry.
help.sketch.circle.three_tangent: Draws a circle that touches three lines, circles or arcs. Use it to fit a circle into the space between three curves, such as the inscribed circle of a triangle.
help.sketch.circle.two_point: Draws a circle from the two ends of its diameter. Use it when the circle's edge points are known rather than its centre.
help.sketch.circle.two_tangent: Draws a circle of a given size that touches two lines, circles or arcs. Use it for a rounding of fixed radius between two curves.
help.sketch.conic: Draws a conic curve between two end points, shaped by an apex point and a rho value. Use it for smooth transitions whose fullness you want to tune, from flat to nearly a sharp corner.
help.sketch.constrainer: Applies the constraint that one or two picked curves nearly have already, such as horizontal, parallel, tangent or equal. Use it to tidy a hand-drawn sketch one relation at a time.
help.sketch.constraint.coincident: Makes a point lie on another point, a curve or a sketch axis. Use it to close gaps in a profile or to put a point on a line.
help.sketch.constraint.collinear: Makes two lines lie on one straight line. Use it to line up interrupted edges, such as both sides of a notch.
help.sketch.constraint.concentric: Gives two circles or arcs the same centre, or centres a circle or arc on a sketch point, including the origin. Pick either pair in either order.
help.sketch.constraint.curvature: Makes two curves that meet at an end point continue with the same curvature (G2). Use it where a tangent join is not smooth enough, for example on visible surfaces.
help.sketch.constraint.equal: Makes lines the same length, or circles and arcs the same radius. Use it so that one dimension drives several matching features.
help.sketch.constraint.fix: Fixes points or curves where they are, or frees them again. Use it for geometry that must not move when you drag or solve the sketch.
help.sketch.constraint.horizontal_vertic: Makes a line, or the line between two points, horizontal or vertical, whichever is closer. Use it to square an outline up to the sketch axes.
help.sketch.constraint.midpoint: Puts a point on the middle of a line, or makes the midpoints of two lines meet. Use it to centre geometry on an edge.
help.sketch.constraint.parallel: Makes two lines parallel. Use it for sides that must stay parallel when other dimensions change.
help.sketch.constraint.perpendicular: Makes two lines meet at a right angle. Use it for square corners between lines that are not on the sketch axes.
help.sketch.constraint.polygon: Makes a closed chain of lines a regular polygon: equal sides, with every corner on one circle. Use it to make a hand-drawn polygon regular and keep it so.
help.sketch.constraint.symmetry: Makes two points or curves mirror each other across a line or about a point. Use it to keep a profile symmetric when you change one side.
help.sketch.constraint.tangent: Makes two curves touch tangentially, such as a line and an arc. Use it for smooth joins without a kink.
help.sketch.construction: Switches curves between normal geometry and construction geometry, which profiles leave out. Use construction curves as helpers for layout, references and dimensions.
help.sketch.construction_line: Create an infinite construction line through two points. Use it to lay out a sketch without splitting profiles.
help.sketch.construction_line.angle: Create an infinite construction line at an angle from sketch X. Pick the point and type the angle, or pick its direction.
help.sketch.construction_line.bisector: Pick two intersecting straight sketch lines, then choose either angle bisector. The result follows its source lines.
help.sketch.construction_line.horizontal: Create an infinite horizontal construction line through a point, or type its distance from the sketch X axis. A typed distance becomes a driving dimension. Its horizontal constraint follows later edits.
help.sketch.construction_line.parallel: Pick a straight sketch line, then place a parallel infinite construction line or type its offset. A typed offset becomes a driving distance. Right-click to choose another reference.
help.sketch.construction_line.perpendicu: Pick a straight sketch line, then place a perpendicular infinite construction line. Right-click to choose another reference.
help.sketch.construction_line.tangent_at: Create a tangent at a point on a circle or circular arc, or an endpoint of an open spline or conic. Pick the curve, then its contact point.
help.sketch.construction_line.tangent_ex: Pick a circle or circular arc, then an external point and a tangent solution. The previews show only contacts on the drawn arc.
help.sketch.construction_line.tangent_tw: Pick two circles or circular arcs, then choose a common tangent in the preview. Contacts must lie on the drawn curves.
help.sketch.construction_line.vertical: Create an infinite vertical construction line through a point, or type its distance from the sketch Y axis. A typed distance becomes a driving dimension. Its vertical constraint follows later edits.
help.sketch.copy: Copies the selected sketch curves and points, together with the constraints and dimensions among them. Paste them into this sketch or another one.
help.sketch.create: Starts a new 2D sketch on a plane or on a flat face of the model. Every extrude, revolve and sweep begins with a sketch.
help.sketch.cut: Copies the selected sketch geometry and deletes it from the sketch, in one undo step. Paste it elsewhere in this sketch or into another one.
help.sketch.dimension: Adds a driving dimension: a length, distance, angle, radius or diameter, depending on what you pick. Type a value or a parameter name, and the sketch follows it.
help.sketch.edit: Opens an existing sketch for editing. The features built on it update when you finish the sketch.
help.sketch.ellipse: Draws an ellipse from its centre, the end of its major axis and a point on its minor side. Use it for oval openings, cams and other elongated round shapes.
help.sketch.equation_curve: Draws a curve from formulas: x(t) and y(t), or y = f(x), over a range. The formulas can use parameters and the curve follows them: use it for a sine wave, a spiral or a gear tooth's involute.
help.sketch.extend: Lengthens a line or arc up to the nearest curve in its way, or grows two curves until they meet. Use it to close gaps in a profile after trimming or editing.
help.sketch.fillet: Rounds the corner where two lines or arcs meet with an arc of a given radius. Several corners rounded together share one radius.
help.sketch.finish: Leaves the sketch and returns to the model. Its closed profiles are then ready for Extrude, Revolve and other features.
help.sketch.finish_auto_constrain: Runs AutoConstrain on the sketch, then finishes it. Use it to leave a sketch fully defined in one step.
help.sketch.fit_curves_to_section: Cuts a mesh or solid body with the sketch plane and fits lines and arcs to the section. Use it to rebuild a scanned or imported part as an editable sketch.
help.sketch.include_3d: Brings model edges, vertices and curves of other sketches into this sketch as linked references, flattening those off its plane onto it. Use it to build on geometry that does not lie in the sketch plane.
help.sketch.infinite: Switches lines between normal lines and infinite construction lines that run across the whole view. Use them as layout references that never end too short.
help.sketch.insert_dxf: Reads the curves of a DXF drawing into a sketch, scaled, turned and placed where you set. Use it to build on a 2D drawing from another program, such as a laser-cut outline.
help.sketch.insert_svg: Reads the paths of an SVG drawing into a sketch, scaled, turned and placed where you set. Use it to turn a logo or vector outline into curves you can extrude.
help.sketch.inspect: Opens a report on the open sketch: how many degrees of freedom are left and whether it is fully constrained. Use it to find out what still moves before you finish the sketch.
help.sketch.intersect: Adds the curves or points where bodies, faces, edges or other sketches cross the sketch plane. They stay linked and follow the model when it changes.
help.sketch.intersection_curve: Creates 3D curves where two bodies or faces meet, linked to them. Use them as paths or guide rails that follow the model.
help.sketch.isoparametric_curve: Creates a 3D curve along a face's U or V direction through a point you pick, linked to the face. Use it as a path or split line that follows the surface.
help.sketch.line: Draws connected lines point by point, as an open chain or a closed outline. It is the basic tool for most profiles.
help.sketch.line.midpoint: Draws a line from its midpoint out to one end, with the other end mirrored. Use it for lines centred on a point, such as a symmetric edge.
help.sketch.line3d: Draws connected straight lines between points in space, with 3D Sketch on. Use it for paths and frames that leave the sketch plane.
help.sketch.mirror: Mirrors sketch curves and points across a line or axis and adds symmetry constraints. Use it to draw half of a symmetric profile and complete it.
help.sketch.move: Moves or rotates sketch curves and points, or a copy of them. Use it to reposition geometry while keeping its shape and constraints.
help.sketch.offset: Creates a copy of a chain of curves at a set distance, on one side or both. Use it for walls, outlines and clearances; the distance stays an editable dimension.
help.sketch.paste: Pastes sketch geometry you copied or cut into the active sketch. Place it at a point or shift it by an offset.
help.sketch.pattern.circular: Copies sketch geometry around a centre point, over a full circle or a set angle. Use it for bolt circles, spokes and teeth.
help.sketch.pattern.rectangular: Copies sketch geometry in rows and columns at set spacings. Use it for grids of holes, slots or vents.
help.sketch.point: Places a sketch point. Use it as a reference for dimensions, constraints, hole centres or later features.
help.sketch.point3d: Places a point in space, with 3D Sketch on. Use it as a reference for 3D curves and paths.
help.sketch.polygon.circumscribed: Draws a regular polygon around a circle, sized from its centre to the middle of a side. Use it when the width across flats is known, as for a hex nut.
help.sketch.polygon.edge: Draws a regular polygon from the two ends of one side. Use it when the length and position of a side are known.
help.sketch.polygon.inscribed: Draws a regular polygon inside a circle, sized from its centre to a corner. Use it when the size across corners is known.
help.sketch.project: Brings model edges, faces, vertices and curves of other sketches into this sketch, projected onto its plane. They stay linked and follow the model when it changes.
help.sketch.project_to_surface: Projects curves of other sketches along this sketch's normal onto a face, as linked 3D curves. Use it to put a logo, split line or path onto a curved surface.
help.sketch.rectangle.center: Draws a rectangle from its centre and one corner. Use it for outlines centred on a point, such as the origin.
help.sketch.rectangle.rounded: Draws a rectangle with all four corners rounded to one radius. Use it for plates, lids and openings with rounded corners.
help.sketch.rectangle.three_point: Draws a rectangle from one edge and a point on the opposite side. Use it for rectangles at an angle to the sketch axes.
help.sketch.rectangle.two_point: Draws a rectangle from two opposite corners. Use it for the outlines of plates, blocks and pockets.
help.sketch.scale: Scales sketch curves and points by a factor about a base point. Use it to resize part of a sketch without drawing it again.
help.sketch.slot.arc_center: Draws a curved slot of a given width along an arc set by its centre, start and end. Use it for adjustment slots around a pivot.
help.sketch.slot.arc_three_point: Draws a curved slot of a given width along an arc through three points. Use it when the slot's path has to pass through given points.
help.sketch.slot.center_point: Draws a straight slot of a given width from its centre to the centre of one end arc. Use it for slots centred on a point.
help.sketch.slot.center_to_center: Draws a straight slot of a given width between the centres of its two end arcs. Use it for slots dimensioned centre to centre, such as adjustment slots for screws.
help.sketch.slot.overall: Draws a straight slot of a given width from one outer end to the other. Use it when the slot's overall length is what matters.
help.sketch.spline.control_point: Draws a cubic spline shaped by control points that it does not pass through. Use it for smooth, flowing curves that you shape by moving the points.
help.sketch.spline.control_point_5: Draws a degree 5 spline shaped by control points. Use it where curves have to join with smoother curvature, for example on visible styled surfaces.
help.sketch.spline.fit_point: Draws a smooth spline that passes through every point you place, open or closed. Use it to trace a shape through known points.
help.sketch.spline3d: Draws a smooth curve in space through points, with 3D Sketch on. Use it for sweep paths and cable runs that leave the sketch plane.
help.sketch.spun_profile: Creates in the sketch plane the outline a body sweeps when it turns about an axis. Use it to get the silhouette of a turned part for a revolve or a drawing.
help.sketch.text: Writes text in the sketch in a chosen font, height and angle; its words can follow parameters. Extrude or emboss it for labels and lettering.
help.sketch.transform: Scales, turns and moves sketch geometry about a centre point in one step. Use it to reposition and resize a selection at once.
help.sketch.trim: Removes the piece of a curve between the nearest crossings around where you click. Use it to clean up overlapping lines into a closed profile.
help.solid.align: Moves the selected bodies so that a point, face or plane on them meets a point, face or plane elsewhere. Use it to place a part against another one without measuring the offset.
help.solid.boundary_fill: Makes solids from the regions enclosed by overlapping tool bodies, filling only the regions you pick. Use it to build a shape from the space that several bodies bound together.
help.solid.bounding_solid: Creates a box that encloses the selected bodies, with an optional margin. Use it to see a part's overall size, or as the stock it is machined from.
help.solid.box: Creates a box from a length, width and height, from a corner point or centred on a point. Use it for a quick block, a placeholder or a body to cut features into.
help.solid.chamfer: Cuts the selected edges with a flat bevel of the distance you set. Use it to break sharp edges or to ease the entry of a pin or screw.
help.solid.coil: Creates a helical body, such as a spring, from a diameter, turns, height or pitch and a round or square section. Use it for springs, coils and helical ridges.
help.solid.combine: Joins bodies, cuts them out of a target body, or keeps only the volume they share, and can keep the tool bodies. Use it to merge parts, to cut one shape with another or to find where two bodies overlap.
help.solid.cone: Creates a cone from a base circle and a height, or a truncated cone when the top has a radius too. Use it for tapers, funnels, countersinks and points.
help.solid.cylinder: Creates a cylinder from a radius or diameter and a height, standing on a point along an axis. Use it for shafts, pins, bosses and round blanks.
help.solid.draft: Tilts the selected faces by the angle you set, measured from a neutral plane. Use it on molded or cast parts so that they slide out of the mold.
help.solid.emboss: Raises sketch profiles, such as text or a logo, out of a face, or sinks them into it. Use it for lettering, labels and markings on flat or round faces.
help.solid.extrude: Pushes a sketch profile into 3D along a distance, adding or removing material. Use it to turn a flat outline into a block, a boss or a pocket.
help.solid.fillet: Rounds the selected edges with a smooth circular blend of the radius you set. Use it to soften sharp edges for strength, comfort or looks.
help.solid.hole: Drills a round hole of the diameter you set at a chosen point on a face. Use it for screw clearances, pins and other simple round openings.
help.solid.loft: Blends a smooth solid between two or more sketch profiles, or from a profile to a point. Use it for transitions, funnels, handles and any shape that changes section along its length.
help.solid.mirror: Makes a mirrored copy of the selected bodies or features across a plane, and can merge it with the original. Use it for symmetric parts, so that you model one half and get both.
help.solid.move: Moves or rotates the selected bodies, or a copy of them, by the distance and angle you set. Use it to reposition a body or to make a second one in another place.
help.solid.offset_face: Pushes the selected faces in or out by the distance you set, and the faces around them follow. Use it to make a wall thicker, a pocket deeper or a boss taller without editing the sketch.
help.solid.pattern.circular: Repeats the selected objects around an axis, for the count and total angle you set. Use it for bolt circles, spokes, fins and teeth.
help.solid.pattern.path: Copies features or bodies along a sketch path, by count and spacing. Use it for holes along a curved edge or parts along a rail.
help.solid.pattern.rectangular: Repeats the selected objects in one or two directions with the count and spacing you set. Use it for rows and grids of holes, ribs, pins or feet.
help.solid.pipe: Creates a round tube along a path of sketch curves, solid or hollow with a wall thickness. Use it for tubes, wires, cables and rails.
help.solid.press_pull: Adds or removes material as you drag a face, or rounds edges as you drag them. Use it for quick changes straight on the model.
help.solid.remove: Takes the selected bodies out of the design from this point in the timeline on; earlier steps keep them. Use it to drop a helper body, such as a cutting tool you no longer need.
help.solid.replace_face: Moves the selected flat faces onto a plane or onto a parallel face, and the body grows or shrinks to meet it. Use it to bring a face flush with another part or a construction plane.
help.solid.revolve: Spins a sketch profile around an axis to make a round solid. Use it for shafts, knobs, bowls and any part that is round about a center line.
help.solid.rib: Adds a thin wall along an open sketch curve, filled out to the next faces of the body. Use it to stiffen walls and corners, for example in moulded or printed parts.
help.solid.scale: Makes the selected bodies larger or smaller by a factor, the same in every direction or one per axis. Use it to resize an imported shape or to allow for shrinkage.
help.solid.shell: Hollows out a solid, leaving walls of the thickness you set, and can open the faces you pick. Use it for boxes, covers and other thin-walled parts.
help.solid.sphere: Creates a sphere from a radius or diameter around a centre point. Use it for balls, knobs and rounded ends.
help.solid.split_body: Cuts a body into separate bodies with a plane, the face of another body or a sketch line. Use it to make parts that are printed, machined or colored on their own.
help.solid.split_face: Divides the selected faces along a plane, the face of another body or sketch curves, without cutting the body. Use it to give part of a face its own draft, color or offset.
help.solid.sweep: Drags a sketch profile along a path to make a solid. Use it for pipes, rails, handles and any part of constant section that follows a curve.
help.solid.thread: Adds an ISO metric thread to a cylindrical face, either as a cosmetic thread or cut into the body. Use it for bolts, threaded holes and printed screw parts.
help.solid.torus: Creates a ring from a major radius around its axis and a minor radius for its round section. Use it for O-rings, handles and round beads.
help.solid.web: Adds a thin wall along each open sketch curve, each filled out to the next faces of the body. Use it for a grid of supporting walls inside housings and trays.
help.surface.blend: Creates a surface that bridges the edges of two bodies, tangent or curvature continuous to both. Use it to join two surfaces smoothly across a gap.
help.surface.boundary: Creates a surface filling a loop of two to four sketch curves, or a network of curves. Use it for free-form panels defined by their edges.
help.surface.extend: Lengthens a surface past its edges, by a distance or up to a plane or face. Use it so that surfaces overlap before you trim or stitch them.
help.surface.extrude: Pushes sketch curves or profiles along a distance into a surface, walls only, without caps. Use it for thin walls and for cutting or splitting tools.
help.surface.fair: Smooths the inside of free-form faces while their edges stay put. Use it to even out bumps and wavy reflections in a surface.
help.surface.loft: Creates a surface that passes through two or more sections in order, without caps. Use it for shells and transitions between different shapes.
help.surface.match: Rebuilds the edge of a surface so it meets another body's edge, with matching tangent or curvature. Use it to close a seam smoothly between two surfaces.
help.surface.offset: Creates a copy of faces at a distance along their normals, as a new surface body. Use it for skins, clearances or the other side of a wall.
help.surface.patch: Fills a sketch region or a closed loop of edges with a face, flat or smoothly curved. Use it to close holes in a surface body.
help.surface.reverse_normal: Turns faces of a surface body over, so their outside faces the other way. Use it before thickening or stitching when the faces point inward.
help.surface.revolve: Turns sketch curves or profiles about an axis into a surface, without caps. Use it for round shells such as lampshades, bowls and nozzles.
help.surface.ruled: Creates a strip of straight lines out from a chain of edges, along the face's normal, tangent or at an angle. Use it for draft walls, run-offs and parting surfaces.
help.surface.stitch: Sews surface bodies together along their shared edges, into a solid when they close. Use it to turn a set of surfaces into one body.
help.surface.sweep: Moves sketch curves or profiles along a path into a surface, without caps. Use it for gutters, trims and other thin shapes that follow a path.
help.surface.thicken: Gives a surface body a thickness, turning it into a solid. Use it to make printable or machinable parts from surfaces.
help.surface.trim: Cuts a surface with a plane, another surface or sketch curves, and keeps the side you pick. Use it to cut surfaces to shape before stitching.
help.surface.unstitch: Separates faces of a body into surface bodies of their own; a solid comes apart into surfaces. Use it to rework single faces of a body.
help.surface.untrim: Removes holes from a face, or restores its outer boundary to the surface's natural bounds. Use it to get back the full surface after a trim.
help.timeline.compute_all: Rebuilds every feature in the timeline from the start. Use it to refresh the model and to see which features fail.
help.timeline.delete: Deletes the selected features from the timeline; deleting a sketch also deletes the features built from it. Use it to remove a step that is no longer wanted.
help.timeline.dependents: Lists the features that would be deleted with a feature, and those that would fail without it. Use it before deleting or changing a feature.
help.timeline.play: Replay the remaining features one at a time, with a half-second pause after each rebuild. Run this command again or press Escape to stop; Go to end jumps immediately.
help.view.apply: Turns the view to a standard direction such as front, top or iso, or to a saved named view. Use it to look at the model from a fixed angle.
help.view.delete: Deletes a saved named view. The model is not changed.
help.view.fit: Zooms and pans so the whole model, or the selection, fills the view. Use it when the model has gone out of sight.
help.view.grid: Shows or hides the grid in the viewport. Use it as a size and orientation guide while modelling.
help.view.ground_shadow: Shows or hides the model's shadow on the ground. Use it to judge height and position more easily.
help.view.home: Turns the view back to the home direction and fits the model. Use it to get back to a known view quickly.
help.view.list: Lists the named views saved in the design. Use it to find a view you saved earlier.
help.view.navigate: Turns, pans or zooms the view by steps, such as a quarter turn left. Use it to move the camera precisely instead of dragging.
help.view.navigation_bar: Shows or hides the navigation bar at the bottom of the viewport. Hide it for more room, show it to reach the view tools by mouse.
help.view.rename: Gives a saved named view a new name. The view itself stays the same.
help.view.save: Saves the current camera position as a named view in the design. Use it to come back to the same angle later, for example for screenshots.
help.view.spin: Orbits the view around the model continuously until the next click or key. Use it to present a model from all sides.
help.view.tool: Latches a camera tool, orbit, pan or zoom, so that dragging with the left mouse button moves the view until you switch it off. Use it on a trackpad or without a middle mouse button.
help.view.visual_style: Switches how the model is drawn: shaded with or without edges, wireframe, or with hidden edges. Use wireframe to see inside, shaded for a clean look.
